name: GO Classes Test Series 2023 | NIELIT Mock Test 5

question.text:
Cooperation between friends stems _______ mutual consideration.

  1. is
  2. out
  3. from
  4. None of these

How many cubes are there in the figure?

  1. $4$
  2. $6$
  3. $8$
  4. $10$

The sum of all natural numbers between $100$ and $200$ which are multiples of $3$ is ____________.

  1. $5000$
  2. $4950$
  3. $4980$
  4. $4900$

The average weight of $5 \mathrm{men}$ is decreased by $3 \mathrm{~kg}$ when one of them weighing $150 \mathrm{~kg}$ is replaced by another person. Find the weight of the new person.

  1. $165$
  2. $135$
  3. $138$
  4. $162$

$$
\frac{1}{1+\log _u^{v w}}+\frac{1}{1+\log _v^{u w}}+\frac{1}{1+\log _w^{u v}}=?
$$

  1. $\log_{10} {uvw}$
  2. $0$
  3. $1$
  4. None of these

A man uses $\dfrac{4}{5}$ of his original speed and he is $12 \mathrm{~min}$ late to reach the destination. Find the correct time to reach the destination if the man is moving at his original speed.

  1. $24 \mathrm{~min}$
  2. $36 \mathrm{~min}$
  3. $48 \mathrm{~min}$
  4. $60 \mathrm{~min}$

Father is aged three times more than his son Sumit. After $8$ years, he would be two and a half times of Sumit's age. After further $8$ years, how many times would he be of Sumit's age?

  1. $2$ times
  2. $2 \dfrac{1}{2}$ times
  3. $2 \dfrac{3}{4}$ times
  4. $3$ times

If $\text{Z}=52$ and $\text{ACT}=48,$ then $\text{BAT}$ will be equal to

  1. $24$
  2. $36$
  3. $46$
  4. $48$

If $31 x+28 y+30 z=365$ then $x+y+z=?$

  1. $12$
  2. $10$
  3. $8$
  4. $6$

If $\left(\dfrac{a}{b}\right)^{x-1}=\left(\dfrac{b}{a}\right)^{x-3},$ then the value of $x$ is:

  1. $\dfrac{1}{2}$
  2. $1$
  3. $2$
  4. $\dfrac{7}{2}$

A man is $24$ years older than his son. In two years, his age will be twice the age of his son. The present age of his son is:

  1. $14$ years
  2. $18$ years
  3. $20$ years
  4. $22$ years

If $x+2y=30,$ then $\left(\dfrac{2y}{5}+\dfrac{x}{3} \right) + \left (\dfrac{x}{5}+\dfrac{2y}{3} \right)$ will be equal to

  1. $8$
  2. $16$
  3. $18$
  4. $20$

How many numbers less than $2^{24}$ are co prime to it?

  1.  $2^{12}$
  2.  $2^{23}$
  3.  $2^{22}$
  4.  None of these

The fourth proportion of $6,11$ and $12$ is ________.

  1. $29$
  2. $23$
  3. $72$
  4. $22$

How many times will the hands of a clock coincide in a day?

  1. $24$
  2. $22$
  3. $20$
  4. $21$

The difference between a two-digit number and the sum of its digits is always a multiple of

  1.  $6$
  2.  $9$
  3.  $11$
  4.  $1$

A metallic sphere of radius $12 \mathrm{~cm}$ is melted and drawn into a wire, whose radius of cross-section is $16 \mathrm{~cm}$. What is the length of the wire?
  1. $45 \mathrm{~cm}$
  2. $27 \mathrm{~cm}$
  3. $9 \mathrm{~cm}$
  4. $18 \mathrm{~cm}$

These questions are based on the following statements.

  • Changes are ideas.
  • No idea is a fancy.
  • Most fancies are images.

If change is an imagination, then which of the following is definitely true?

  1.  Few imaginations are images.
  2.  Few imaginations are not fancies.
  3.  Few images are not imaginations.
  4.  Few images are imaginations.

If $50 \%$ of $(p-q)=30 \%$ of $(p+q),$ then $p:q$ is ________.

  1. $5: 3$
  2. $4: 1$
  3. $3: 5$
  4. $1: 4$

$5$ skilled workers can build a wall in $20$ days: $8$ semi-skilled workers can build a wall in $25$ days; $10$ unskilled workers can build a wall in $30$ days. If a team has $2$ skilled, $4$ semi-skilled and $5$ unskilled workers, how long will it take to build the wall?

  1. $\dfrac{300}{19}$ days
  2. $\dfrac{300}{17}$ days
  3. $\dfrac{300}{15}$ days
  4. None

It was Sunday on Jan $1, 2006.$ What was the day of the week Jan $1, 2010?$

  1. Sunday
  2. Saturday
  3. Friday
  4. Wednesday

Observe the given line chart, which contains the data of passengers who travelled from Bangalore to Mumbai(in thousands).

The total number of male passengers who travel on Tuesday and Wednesday is approximately how much $\%$ more than the number of male passengers who travel on Thursday?

  1. $15\%$
  2. $50\%$
  3. $33.33\%$
  4. $75\%$

A car travels $1 / 3$ of the distance on a straight road with a velocity of $10 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$, the next $1 / 3$ with a velocity of $20 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ and the last $1 / 3$ with a velocity of $60 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$. What is the average velocity of the car for the whole journey?
  1. $18 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$
  2. $10 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$
  3. $20 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$
  4. $15 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$

The last day of a century cannot be

  1. Monday
  2. Wednesday
  3. Tuesday
  4. Friday

One evening Dinesh and Swetha sat in a park such that their backs are towards each other. If Dinesh’s shadow is falling to his left then which direction is Swetha facing?

  1.  North-east
  2.  North
  3.  East
  4.  South
If a mirror is placed on the line MN then which of the answer figure is the right image of the given figure?

Rajesh found a decimal number which when represented in bases $2, 3, 4, 5,$ and $6$ ends in $1, 2, 3, 4$ and $5$ respectively. What is the smallest positive integer satisfying this property?

  1. $60$
  2. $59$
  3. $780$
  4. $960$

Five persons $\text{P, Q, R, S}$ and $\text{T}$ are standing in a queue. $\text{‘R'}$ in standing between $\text{‘P'}$ and $\text{T. ‘P'}$ is just behind $\text{‘Q', Q}$ is second in the queue. Who is $2^{\text {nd }}$ last in the queue?

  1. $\text{T}$
  2. $\text{S}$
  3. $\text{R}$
  4. $\text{P}$

Which of the following is true?

  1. $\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{7}=\sqrt{10}$
  2. $\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{7}\leq \sqrt{10}$
  3. $\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{7}< \sqrt{10}$
  4. $\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{7}> \sqrt{10}$

If it _______ winter, all these trees would be covered in snow.

  1. was
  2. were
  3. would be
  4. would have been

How many factors of $1800$ are divisible by $10?$

  1. $100$
  2. $18$
  3. $180$
  4. None of these

From a point $\text{P}$ on the ground the angle of elevation of the top of a $10 \mathrm{~m}$ tall building is $30^{\circ}$. A flag is hoisted at the top of the building and the angle of elevation of the top of the flagstaff from P is $45^{\circ}$. Find the length of the flagstaff and the distance of the building from the point $\text{P}.$

  1. $7.32 \mathrm{~m}$
  2. $8.45 \mathrm{~m}$
  3. $7.16 \mathrm{~m}$
  4. $8.32 \mathrm{~m}$

$\text{A}$ is thrice as efficient as $\text{B}$ and can finish the task $16$ days ahead of $\text{B}.$ Find the number of days required to finish the same task, if both are working alternately starting from $\text{A}.$

  1. $6$ days
  2. $8$ days
  3. $10$ days
  4. $12$ days

The cost of production of a cordless phone set in $2002$ is Rs. $900,$ divided between material, labour and overheads in the ratio $3 : 4: 2$. If the cordless phone set is marked at a price that gives a $20 \%$ profit on the component of price accounted for by labour, what is the marked price of the set?

  1. Rs. $980$
  2. Rs. $1080$
  3. Rs. $960$
  4. None of these

$3$ women and $2$ men are to be selected from $6$ women and $5$ men to constitute a committee. There are $2$ women who could not be on the same committee. Find the number of such committees.

  1. $40$
  2. $160$
  3. $200$
  4. $150$

A certain sum was borrowed $x$ years ago at $20 \%$ p.a simple interest. If at present, the principal is $300 \%$ more than the interest, what percentage will it be of the interest $23 / 4$ years from now?

  1. $100$
  2. $55$
  3. $120$
  4. $125$

What are you listening?
  1. to
  2. On
  3. with
  4. about

If time is $6: 10,$ find angle between minute hand and hour hand?

  1. $90^{\circ}$
  2. $120^{\circ}$
  3. $125^{\circ}$
  4. $60^{\circ}$

$\text{A's}$ expenditure and savings are in the ratio $5:3.$ If her income increases by $12 \%$ and expenditure by $15 \%,$ then by how much percent do her savings increase?

  1. $12$
  2. $7$
  3. $8$
  4. $13$

How is my father’s mother’s only daughter-in-law’s sister related to me?

  1. Aunt
  2.  Sister
  3.  Cousin
  4.  Niece

Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to that expressed in the main pair.
$$\text{OUTSKIRTS : TOWN : : }$$

  1. rung : ladder
  2. trunk : tree
  3. water : goblet
  4. margin : page

These questions are based on the following statements.

  • Changes are ideas.
  • No idea is a fancy.
  • Most fancies are images.

Which of the following statement contradicts the conclusion of the above three statements?

  1.  Few images are changes
  2.  No image is change.
  3.  All changes are not images.
  4.  All images are changes.

The $\text{Q}$-factor of a parallel resonant circuit with a damping factor of $0.5$ is ______________.

  1. $1$
  2. $3$
  3. $5$
  4. $0.25$

What is the asymptotic order of the given function
$$F(n) = 2F(n/2) + (n-2)$$

  1. $\Theta(n)$
  2. $\Theta(\log n)$
  3. $\Theta(n \log n)$
  4. $\Theta(n^2)$

Load factor is defined as $(m/n)$ where $n$ is the total size of the hash table and $m$ is the preferred number of entries which can be inserted before a increment in size of the underlying data structure is required.

A hash table has $1000$ slots and $200$ items have already been hashed in it. What is the load factor?

  1. $5$
  2. $1$
  3. $0.5$
  4. $0.2$

The equivalent resistance shown in the figure is _________ (in ohms)

  1. $1$
  2. $2$
  3. $3$
  4. $4$

Find the running time complexity of the given program.

for(int i=0;i<n;i++) {
    for(int j=0;j<n*n;j++) {
        // O(1) work
    }
}
  1. $\Theta(1)$
  2. $\Theta(n)$
  3. $\Theta(n^2)$
  4. $\Theta(n^3)$

Which of the following operations are not suitable for linked list?

  1. Insertion sort
  2. Binary search
  3. Radix sort
  4. Polynomial manipulation

Find the number of possibilities to choose a primary key of the relation $\text{R(A, B, C, D, E)}$.

  1. $ 5$
  2. $ 25$
  3. $ 31$
  4. $ 120$

In a circular linked list, insertion of a record involves modification of

  1. One pointer
  2. Two pointers
  3. Three pointers
  4. No pointers

Which of the following expressions does not represent the logical complement (negation) of $x?$

  1.  $x$ NAND $x$
  2.  $x$ NOR $x$
  3.  $x$ NAND $1$
  4.  $x$ NOR $1$

A frequency modulated signal can be demodulated by:
  1. Multiplying with carrier frequency followed by low pass filtering
  2. Passing through a Voltage Controlled Oscillator [VCO]
  3. Passing through an differentiator followed by Envelope Detection
  4. Passing through an Integrator followed by Envelope Detection.

Consider an $\text{AM}$ signal given by
$$
s(t)=4 \operatorname{Cos}(3800 \pi t)+16 \operatorname{Cos}(4000 \pi t)+4 \operatorname{Cos}(4200 \pi t) \text {. }
$$
The power efficiency of the modulation scheme is

  1. $\dfrac{1}{9}$
  2. $\dfrac{1}{6}$
  3. $\dfrac{1}{3}$
  4. $\dfrac{1}{18}$

A certain family has $6$ children, consisting of $3$ boys and $3$ girls. Assuming that all birth orders are equally likely, what is the probability that the $3$ eldest children are the $3$ girls?

  1. $0.03$
  2. $0.04$
  3. $0.05$
  4. $0.08$

Which of the following is the correct recursive equation for the following sequence. (Assume the base conditions)
$$\{1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, \dots\}$$
  1. $T(n) = T(n-1) + 1$
  2. $T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2)$
  3. $(T(n) = T(n-2) + 1$
  4. None of the above

Which of the following are equivalent to the statement?

int  k=(i<<4)+(j>>2)

  1.  int k=i * 16+j / 4; 
  2. int k=i * 8+j * 2;

  3.  int k=i * 3+j / 2;

  4.  int k=i / 8+j * 4;

Find the correct output of the given program.

#include<stdio.h>
int main(){
     int a[5] = {4, 6, 8, 0, 3};
     int i, n=5, m = 0, c=0;
     
     for(i=0;i<=n-1;i++){
         if(a[i]==m){
            c=1;
            break;
         }
     }
     if(c==0)
        printf("The number is in the list");
     else
        printf("The number is not in the list");
     return 0;
}
  1. The number is in the list
  2. The number is not in the list
  3. Compiler error
  4. Runtime error

A crime is committed by one of two suspects, $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$. Initially, there is equal evidence against both of them. In further investigation at the crime scene, it is found that the guilty party had a blood type found in $10\%$ of the population. Suspect $\text{A}$ does match this blood type, whereas the blood type of Suspect $\text{B}$ is unknown. What is the probability that $\text{A}$ is the guilty party?

  1. $10/11$
  2. $11/10$
  3. $11/5$
  4. $5/11$

In a pipelined RISC computer where all arithmetic instructions have the same CPI (cycles per instruction), which of the following actions would improve the execution time of a typical program?
  1. Increasing the clock cycle rate
  2. Disallowing any forwarding in the pipeline
  3. Doubling the sizes of the instruction cache and the data
cache without changing the clock cycle time
 
  1. I only
  2. II only
  3. III only
  4. I and III

We are interested in forming $3$ letter words $\text{(“3-words”)}$ using the letters in $\text{LITTLEST}.$ For the purposes of the problem, a $\text{“word”}$ is any ordered list of letters. How many words can be made with no repeated letters?

  1. $50$
  2. $60$
  3. $70$
  4. $80$

Given the production rules of a grammar $\text{G1}$ as

  • $S_1 \rightarrow AB \mid aaB$
  • $A \rightarrow a \mid Aa$
  • $B \rightarrow b$

and the production rules of a grammar $\text{G2}$ as

  • $S_2 \rightarrow aS_2bS_2  \mid bS_2 aS_2 \mid \lambda$

Which of the following is the correct statement?

  1. $\text{G1}$ is ambiguous and $\text{G2}$ is not ambiguous
  2. $\text{G1}$ is ambiguous and $\text{G2}$ is ambiguous
  3. $\text{G1}$ is not ambiguous and $\text{G2}$ is ambiguous
  4. $\text{G1}$ is not ambiguous and $\text{G2}$ is not ambiguous

Consider the two statements given below.

  • $\textbf{Statement 1: }$ If we add an edge to a MST, the resulting subgraph is still a MST.
  • $\textbf{Statement 2: }$ If there are $V$ vertices in a given graph, a MST of that graph contains $|V|-1$ edges.

Which of the following is correct?

  1. Statement $1$ is TRUE and Statement $2$ is TRUE.
  2. Statement $1$ is TRUE and Statement $2$ is FALSE.
  3. Statement $1$ is FALSE and Statement $2$ is TRUE.
  4. Statement $1$ is FALSE and Statement $2$ is FALSE.

Inherited attributes are attributes at a node whose dependency is ___________.

  1. Restricted to siblings
  2. Restricted to parent
  3. Both A and B
  4. Neither A nor B

Find the running time complexity of the following recursive equations.
$$5T(n/2) + \Theta(n^2)$$

  1. $\Theta(n^2)$
  2. $\Theta(n^{\log_2 5})$
  3. $\Theta(n.n^{\log_2 5})$
  4. None of the above.

In $\text{LR(1)}$ parsing, what constitutes a shift/reduce conflict?

  1. A $\text{DFA}$ state contains both $\text{LR}$ items allowing shift and reduce for the different lookahead.
  2. A $\text{DFA}$ state contains both $\text{LR}$ items allowing shift and reduce for the same lookahead.
  3. A $\text{DFA}$ state contains both $\text{LR}$ items allowing shifts for the same lookahead.
  4. A $\text{DFA}$ state contains both $\text{LR}$ items allowing shifts for the different lookahead.

In a database file structure, the search key field is $14$ bytes long, the block size is $1024$ bytes, a record pointer is $7$ bytes and a block point is $12$ bytes. The largest possible order of a non-leaf node is a $\mathrm{B}^{+}$tree implementing this file structure is _________.

  1. $ 23$
  2. $ 24$
  3. $ 34$
  4. $ 39$

Which of the following statements is/are true?

  1. Every view serializable schedule is also conflict serializable.
  2. Every conflict serializable schedule is also view serializable.
  3. Some view serializable schedules are conflict serializable.
  4. No view serializable schedule is conflict serializable.

 

  1.  Statement $1$ only.
  2.  Statements $2$ and $3$ only.
  3.  Statements $1$ and $4$ only.
  4.  Statements $2$ and $4$ only.

If a high $\mathrm{Q}$ parallel resonant circuit is load with a resistance then
  1. The circuit impedance reduces
  2. The resonant frequency remains the same
  3. The bandwidth reduces
  4. The bandwidth increases

Find the correct output of the given program.

#include<stdio.h>
void main() {
    int disp[2][4] = { 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17};
    printf("%d %d", disp[1][2], *(*(disp+1)+2));
}
  1. $15\; 16$
  2. $12\; 16$
  3. $16\; 16$
  4. Compiler error

Three people are running for student government. There are $202$ people who vote. What is the minimum number of votes needed for someone to win the election?

  1. $66$
  2. $67$
  3. $68$
  4. $69$

A bag contains one marble which is either green or blue, with equal probabilities. A green marble is put in the bag (so there are $2$ marbles now), and then a random marble is taken out. The marble taken out is green. What is the probability that the remaining marble is also green?

  1. $1/2$
  2. $2/3$
  3. $2/5$
  4. $1/5$

Which of the following benefits does micro-programming offer?

  1. Allows implementation of more complex instructions
  2. Enables more primitive than assembly programming
  3. Reduces field changes to defect
  4. All of the above

A city with $6$ districts has $6$ robberies in a particular week. Assume the robberies are located randomly, with all possibilities for which robbery occurred where equally likely. What is the probability that some district had more than $1$ robbery?

  1. $0.89$
  2. $0.98$
  3. $0.81$
  4. $0.94$

Consider the two statements given below.

  • $\textbf{Statement 1: }$ For every $n$ there exists a directed graph on $n$ vertices with $\Omega(n^2)$ edges that has a topological ordering.
  • $\textbf{Statement 2: }$ In a connected weighted graph, the edge with maximum weight is never in the minimum spanning tree.

Which of the following is correct?

  1. Statement $1$ is TRUE and Statement $2$ is TRUE.
  2. Statement $1$ is TRUE and Statement $2$ is FALSE.
  3. Statement $1$ is FALSE and Statement $2$ is TRUE.
  4. Statement $1$ is FALSE and Statement $2$ is FALSE.

How many ways are there to seat $10$ people, consisting of $5$ couples, in a row of seats $(10$ seats wide) if the seats are assigned at random?

  1. $8!$
  2. $9!$
  3. $10!$
  4. None of the above

Assertion (A): The following schedule is not conflict serializable schedule.

Reason (R): There is not any cycle in this schedule.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline \text { Time } & T_1 & T_2 & T_3 \\
\hline & & & R(D) \\
 & & R(A) & \\ 
& R(C) & & \\
& & W(A) & \\
& & R(B) & \\
& & R(C) & \\
& & & R(E) \\
&R(A) &  & \\
& & & R(B) \\
& & R(D) & \\
&W(A) &  & \\
& &  & W(B) \\
&R(E) &  & \\ \hline
\end{array}$$

 

A.  Both $(A)$ and $(R)$ are true and $(R)$ is the correct reason for $(A). $

B.  Both $(A)$ and $(R)$ are true but $(R)$ is not the correct reason for $(A). $

C.  Both $(A)$ and $(\mathrm{R})$ are false

D.  $(A)$ is true but $(R)$ is false

In the given sequential circuit, the circuit's initial state, before the first clock pulse, is $\text{Q}_1 \text{Q}_0 = 00$. Determine the state $\left(\text{Q}_1 \text{Q}_0\right)$ immediately after the $333$rd clock pulse.

Let $\text{A}=11111010$ and $\text{B}=00001010$ be two $8$-bit $2$'s complement numbers. Their product in $2$'s complement is _______.

  1. $11000100$
  2.  $10011100$
  3.  $10100101$
  4.  $11010101$

The input-output relationship of a system is given by $y(t)=x\left(t^2\right)$. Then the system is
  1. Linear system and static system
  2. Linear system and dynamic system
  3. Time invariant and causal system
  4. Non-linear and time variant system

$\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{A} \mid \mathrm{A}$ or $\mathrm{A}|(\mathrm{A})|$ true $\mid$ false

Which of the following is false about the First sets for each production and nonterminal?

  1. $\operatorname{FIRST( true)}=\{\text{“true"} \}$
  2. $\operatorname{FIRST(false)} =\{\text{“false"} \}$
  3. $\operatorname{FIRST}(\mathrm{A})=\{\text{“("\}}$
  4. $\operatorname{FIRST}(\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{A})=\mathrm{FIRST}(\mathrm{A}$ or $\mathrm{A})=\operatorname{FIRST}(\mathrm{A})=\{\text{“true", “false"} \}$

Consider the array A = $\{20, 15, 18, 7, 9, 5, 12, 3, 6, 2\}$, which of the following is correct?
  1. Given array is a min-heap.
  2. Given array is max-heap.
  3. Given array is neither max-heap nor min-heap.
  4. None of the above.

The density function of a random variable $X$ is given by
$$f(x) = \left\{\begin{matrix}
    \dfrac{1}{2}x &; 0 \\   0 &; \text{otherwise}
\end{matrix}\right. $$
Find the expected value of $X$.

  1. $2/3$
  2. $1$
  3. $4/3$
  4. $5/3$

The average memory access time for a machine with a cache hit rate of $95 \%$ where the cache access time is $10 \mathrm{~ns}$ and the memory access time is $100 \mathrm{~ns}$ is _______.

  1.  $55 \mathrm{~ns}$
  2.  $45 \mathrm{~ns}$
  3.  $90 \mathrm{~ns}$
  4.  $19.5 \mathrm{~ns}$

Consider the two statements given below.

  • $\textbf{Statement 1: }$ A MST contains a cycle.
  • $\textbf{Statement 2: }$ If we remove an edge from a MST, the resulting sub-graph is still a MST.

Which of the following is correct?

  1. Statement $1$ is TRUE and Statement $2$ is TRUE.
  2. Statement $1$ is TRUE and Statement $2$ is FALSE.
  3. Statement $1$ is FALSE and Statement $2$ is TRUE.
  4. Statement $1$ is FALSE and Statement $2$ is FALSE.

Which of the following options represents the correct output program given below?

#include <stdio.h>
int main() {
    int arr[5] = {42, 10, 38, 56, 99};
    for(int i=0;i<5;i++) {
        for(int j=i+1;j<5;j++) {
            if(arr[i]>arr[j]) {
                int temp = arr[i];
                arr[i] = arr[j];
                arr[j] = temp;
            }
        }
    }
    for(int i=0;i<5;i++) {
        printf("%d ", arr[i]);
    }
}
  1. $38\; 10 \;42 \;56\; 99$
  2. $10\; 38\; 42 \;56\; 99$
  3. $10\; 38\; 42 \;99\; 56$
  4. $10\; 42 \;38 \;99\; 56$

How many four-digit numbers exist such that their digits are in strictly increasing order?
